utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Ninkovic, the date is the 4th of December, 1992. Obviously it is the command of the 2nd Posavina Brigade that sent this letter. Just tell me one thing: Is this a letter that you received from the command of the 2nd Posavina Brigade?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: If there is no objection from our colleagues, I would like to admit this into evidence. MR. DI FAZIO: No objection at all.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit D32/4 and D32/4 ter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. Cross-examination by the Prosecution? Yes, Mr. Di Fazio? You can start your cross-examination. MR. DI FAZIO: I can, yes. Cross-examined by Mr. Di Fazio:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ninkovic, I just want to ask you some questions regarding your background. Am I correct that you have no formal training as a lawyer?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are not quite right, because I passed the state examination, which means that I had to have certain knowledge in the field of the law.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: State examination in what?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For working in the state administration. That means knowing the constitution, the system of state administration, administration procedure, those are legal matters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. That was legal training directed towards enabling to you carry out your duties at the Ministry of Defence, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That was not training. That was an examination with five professors there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you a lawyer or not?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not a lawyer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it's fair to say, therefore, that you lack any expertise in matters of constitutional law?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a broad-based question but I am familiar with the constitution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, I think maybe we all understand what this means because he has talked about his training, the constitution of his country, but your question does not pertain to comparative constitutional theory or practice. MR. DI FAZIO: No, it doesn't. That's as far as I need to go I just wanted to establish that point because of a matter raised by Mr. Weiner before the break. I just wanted to make it clear what his expertise or knowledge of the law was. I'll now abandon the topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said in your evidence in chief that you joined the SDS in 1993 or 1994. Can you be a little bit more precise as to when you did in fact join the -- that party?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have a membership card of the Serb Democratic Party from 1995. I can show it as a document. But I cannot define the exact date. This was between 1993 and 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could it have been 1993, therefore?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, possibly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could it have been early 1993?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. Only the end.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why? Why do you say that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said that I became a member of the Serb Democratic Party between 1993 and 1994, January is not a transition month in the terms of the -- in terms of the following year. It's not like December. December is the last month of the year. According to the calendar that I am aware of.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There would be nothing to prevent you joining the SDS in January of any year, would there?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand that question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I won't pursue it. What was your reason for leaving the Liberal Party, I think it was, and joining the SDS?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This party no longer existed in Republika Srpska. Secondly, the state in which I entered the Liberal Party ceased to exist. It is much harder to change a state than a party. I would have liked to have remained in Yugoslavia and to have remained a member of the Liberal Party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there something in the policies of the SDS that appealed to you?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What would you say that was?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The right of peoples to self-determination which was enshrined in the SFRY constitution as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that right was applied to non-Serb persons as well?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The right to self-determination was one of the principles in the SFRY constitution. It was used by the people of the SFRY, peoples. So the Serbs and Croats and Slovenians and Macedonians and Montenegrins and the Muslims enjoyed this right equally. Those were the peoples of the SFRY.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And are you still a member of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You have heard, I take it, of various organisations known as SAOs and in particular two, the SAO of Northern Bosnia and the SAO of Semberija and Majevica. You've heard of those entities, those regional organs of government?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about that but then I did not have detailed information because I was not in the fora where I could have heard about that in greater detail, and more precisely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I suggested to you that the SAO of Northern Bosnia later became, in fact, the SAO of Semberija and Majevica, would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. Could you please repeat the question? I didn't catch the second part of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll do that. The SAO of Northern Bosnia later, in fact, transformed itself into the SAO of Semberija and Majevica, that is correct, is it not?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know which regions they covered?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Geographically, yes. I know the geography of the former Yugoslavia and Bosnia-Herzegovina, which is the republic where I'm living, and that's a territory covering -- should I now list the names and regions?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, no. I'm not asking you to did that. I'm just asking you a simple question. Are you aware of the territory governed or covered by the SAO of Northern Bosnia and, if you are, was that the same territory covered or administered by the SAO Semberija and Majevica?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the geographical sense I know that area. However, as for the politics, I can't say the same.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry, I don't want to dwell on this topic but I still don't understand what you're saying. Are you saying that geographically the SAO of Northern Bosnia and the SAO of Semberija and Majevica governed the same geographical area?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't say that. I said that I know the geography. I know what the Northern Bosnia is and where it is. However, I said that in the political sense, I don't know if it covered the same area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you say that the SAO of Northern Bosnia was the first to come into existence, followed by the SAO of Semberija and Majevica? In other words, one followed the other?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard of these notions. However, I told you that I was not a member of fora where I could have learned about this in greater depth; therefore, I don't know the dates. I don't know the decisions that were passed. As a citizen, yes, I've heard about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you for those preliminary matters. I just turn to another topic now. I want to ask you about the Crisis Staff and the War Presidency and later the Municipal Assembly of -- the Serbian Municipal Assembly of Bosanski Samac. Would you agree with me that the Crisis Staff for the period that it operated was in fact the highest civilian authority in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you are referring to the Crisis Staff substituting the municipality -- the Municipal Assembly, then in that sense, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would it be your position that the Crisis Staff in its activities in 1992, endeavoured, as far as possible, to look after the health and welfare of the population living in the municipality?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have to make a distinction between the executive branch, meaning the executive council, its powers on one hand, and the Crisis Staff on the other hand. The normal procedure is to have the executive council as the government of the municipality to possess a number of powers in the area of economy, utilities, and everything that is needed in order to create good living conditions for residents of a municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about the actual mechanics of government. I'm asking you a very simple question. Would you agree with me that the Crisis Staff had, as one of its primary concerns, the health and safety and welfare of citizens in the area it administered?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it is looked at as an individual organ, then yes, it had the responsibilities in the areas that you have mentioned. However, that is a kind of -- that is a sort of a separatist point of view, because the government, in principle, is a single institution. That is a principle set forth in the constitution.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not asking for fine distinctions, Mr. Ninkovic. It's just a very simple proposition. The Crisis Staff was concerned with the health and welfare and well-being of people who lived in the area it administered. Surely that was its principal -- one of its principal concerns, and a principal concern of all good government everywhere.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am president of the Municipal Assembly, and I know what the responsibilities of the Municipal Assembly. If we say that the Crisis Staff had certain responsibilities while the Municipal Assembly wasn't functioning, then it is quite clear what those responsibilities and powers were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I understand that and I understand that the Crisis Staff didn't deal with foreign policy, for example, but in the framework of its responsibilities, it acted as best it could, is this your position, for the safety and welfare and health and well-being of the citizens living in the territory it administered?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Every government based on democracy and rule of law works on the basis of those principles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it your position that that concern was extended to non-Serbs as well, Croats and the Muslims, living in the town and in the municipality?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Somebody who was a member of the Crisis Staff would be better positioned to answer this question. However, I know that the Crisis Staff endeavoured to work along the lines described by you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the same considerations applied to the civilian authorities throughout the period of time following April the 16th and 17th in their various incarnations, that is, as the Crisis Staff, as the War Presidency, and later as the Serbian Municipal Assembly of Bosanski Samac; is that your position?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a very broad question. Could you be more concise and specific.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With respect, it's not that broad. It's a very simple proposition. As far as possible, the Crisis Staff, later the War Presidency, and later the Serbian municipality of Bosanski Samac, were concerned to maintain the health, safety and welfare of all citizens, so far as possible, so far as it could operate?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We are not getting translation. MR. DI FAZIO: No.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the answer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can you please start your answer all over again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In times of war, authorities have significantly fewer possibilities to do what can be done in peace time for the welfare of residents of a municipality or of a region, due to the war itself. Therefore, there are fewer resources, there is a greater danger of getting killed, and everything else that naturally comes with war. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I've got no quarrel with that. I understand your position perfectly well, but that's not really my question. It's not my question. You see, all I'm asking you is that those concerns for the health and safety and welfare of all citizens existed all the way through the municipal administration - that's your position - in the Crisis Staff, the War Presidency, and later the Serbian municipality of -- Serbian Assembly in the municipality of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already answered that question. Every government based on democracy and rule of law has these principles implemented in its work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, particularly in these trying times of war, one of the main tools that civilian authorities have in order to bring about the health and safety and well-being of their citizens, as far as possible, is information. So the Crisis Staff and later the War Presidency and later the Municipal Assembly of Bosanski Samac needed to be told, kept informed, of what was going on in the municipality, the concerns of the citizens, problems of the citizens, difficulties that citizens might be encountering, that sort of thing?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I understood you well, you are saying that institutions and organs of authorities have to have necessary information at their disposal in order to govern in a municipality. We have to make a distinction here between what is a cooperation between certain organs, which is regulated by the law on state administration on one hand, and information as a public matter on the other hand, such as media, informing the population and so on. This is how I understood your question. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me rephrase it and perhaps I can assist you. It was important, wasn't it, for the Crisis Staff and the War Presidency and the municipal assembly to be kept informed of conditions on the ground in the town and municipality of Bosanski Samac, particularly in times of war?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Any institution or organ in a municipality has its own sources of information in their particular field. So all of that information put together is a basis used for decision-making, and this is something that has to do with the system of state administration.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's right. And various organs of administration, various entities in the municipal administration had to keep the Crisis Staff informed about what they were up to, what they were doing, difficulties they were experiencing, conditions on the ground? They had to tell the Crisis Staff what was going on. Otherwise the Crisis Staff wouldn't know what to do. That's, as a general proposition, correct, is it not?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spoke about the system-based law, and how it is to be interpreted. Practice is another matter. I don't know whether administrative organs and other institutions informed the Crisis Staff about their work. This would best be explained by officials from those organs and members of the Crisis Staff. That's logical.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Can the witness be shown Exhibit P112, please? Perhaps it should be P112 ter, the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you have that document? Thank you. Could you please --

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please have a look at Article 1, the second paragraph. It deals with the executive board.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a minute, please. I need to read this through.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read Article 1 of this decision.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And second paragraph is very simple and plain, is it not? It says, "That the executive board has to report to the Crisis Staff on all aspects of social life, implementation of policies, decisions and other regulations." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the executive board was feeding information about life and conditions in Bosanski Samac to the Crisis Staff, was it not?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a legal provision. This is based on the law. Now, as to whether the executive council acted in accordance with this, this is a question that you should put to the president of the executive council. That has to do with practice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you a member of the executive board?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1993, pursuant to the Statute of Samac Municipal Assembly, I was ex officio member, meaning not a permanent member, but when the executive council discussed matters that had to do with defence -- may I continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, you may. You can complete your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Therefore, in 1993, ex officio, as a chief of the defence department, I was member of executive council but not a permanent member. I was only invited to attend sessions when certain matters that had to do with defence were on the agenda. And these matters were also linked to the functioning of the economy. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. On the 28th of March, 1992, didn't the Municipal Assembly of Samac and Pelagicevo, under formation, pass a decision electing members of the executive council, and it made Mirko Jovanovic President, Milos Bogdanovic Secretary of the municipal Secretariat of National Defence and it made you Deputy Secretary of the municipal Secretariat of the National Defence?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That executive council did not function, and in practice, I did not discharge that duty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. So they just passed a decision setting up an executive board, nominating all these people, and it never functioned, never operated, is that your position?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was never invited to attend, nor did I participate in the work of that organ, and as far as I know, there were no sessions whatsoever. There was a very brief period of time before the beginning of the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So was the decision invalid or worthless? Is that your position?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it was not implemented, then yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One of the other members of this phantom body was Stevan Todorovic, was it not?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The name -- the names of members of that executive council that didn't function are familiar to me from the Official Gazette.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Well, we'll return to that later. Can I ask you to turn your attention back to P112, please, you see the decision on the executive board and administrative bodies. That's dated the 30th of May, 1992, is it not?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are now referring to the document that's on the ELMO; is that right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. The decision on the executive board and administrative bodies, Exhibit P112. It's dated 30th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that's the document, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So at least at the 30th of May, 1992, there was a contemplation that the executive board would perform some function, that must be so, otherwise what's the point of passing another phantom decision?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like a clarification of the term "phantom," because maybe this witness could be confused. What -- in which sense my friend is using it. MR. DI FAZIO: I'll rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Hollow or meaningless. Do you want me to repeat my question?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understood what you meant. I think that this executive council, which, as you say, was established on the 20 something March, I didn't remember the date, didn't work. I was never invited to attend any sessions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that. I understand what your position is. You've explained yourself very clearly. Thank you very much. My question is this: This document deals with the functioning of the executive board and administrative bodies. It sets out clear regulations dealing with its functioning and its dated the 30th of May. Can you think of any reason as to why this would have been passed, this decision would have been taken, if the executive board was not in fact functioning?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will tell you what my opinion is. The title, the heading here, "The Crisis Staff" indicates -- or rather the Crisis Staff realised that the executive organ should be established, having the powers that normally belonged to the executive organs and that has to do with the various structures in the municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Go to the back of the document. It's the end of the document. It's signed by Blagoje Simic, Dr. Blagoje Simic, and you see the end, Article 19, and then you see, "CC." And the document is CCed or sent to the files of the Crisis Staff and the files of the executive board. Now, if there is no executive board functioning, why would the document be sent to its files?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think we understand each other. I am talking about the executive council not functioning in March. In March of 1992. This decision here was passed later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. It was passed in May of 1992. We can see that on the front of the document, can you not?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. This executive council did function.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me be as simple as I possibly can. When did an executive council or an executive board, call it what you will, start to operate in the municipality of Bosanski Samac? Obviously I mean a Serbian executive board.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometime in June of 1992. That was June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But this document is dated the 30th of May. It must have been operating in May, surely?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, no. And I've told you that several times already.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. What about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Ninkovic, Mr. Di Fazio had mentioned earlier that the document was copied to the files of the executive board. I'm just wondering if there wasn't a functioning executive board, how come it had files? And paper was being filed away, such as this particular document. I have a little bit of confusion with this, frankly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have understood your question. That question pertains to the way an office functions. Office functioning defines how archives are kept. So archives of the executive council are kept where the archives from -- archives from 1986, 1987, 1988 are kept. This is a place, this is a room, this is a shelf, where it says "executive council." So regardless of which particular executive board and at which point in time one is referring to, that is where these documents are kept. If we need documents from the executive board in 1982 or 1981, we will come to that particular room, that particular shelf, and we are going to find the documents there. That is called the way an office operates. This is a purely administrative matter. This is a purely technical thing. Office management. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But her honour's question was -- didn't require that sort of answer, with respect. It's a very simple question. I want to put it to you again. The document presupposes the existence of files of an executive board, because it says that this document, this piece of paper, this decision, this P112, has to be filed. Now if it has to be filed, there must be somewhere to file it, correct? And if it describes that place as the files of the executive board, there must be an executive board. That's just pure logic, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is logic, but there can be certain pauses in the operation of an institution. For example, when a term of office expires for one particular set of people, then for a while there is a pause and then there can be another set of people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the scenario is, as far as an executive board is concerned, that in March of 1992, the Serbian municipality of Bosanski Samac and Pelagicevo in formation, held its meeting, appointed an executive board, provided a whole list of members of that executive board, of which you were a member, but it never existed, it didn't actually function, didn't carry out any duties, conduct meetings, anything like that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, what you read, that is this executive board, that did not meet, or rather, at least, I don't know of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, you agree with the -- that you were in fact appointed to in March of 1992, albeit that you say it never actually functioned?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I learned about that from Mr. Milos Bogdanovic, and much later, I saw it in the Official Gazette.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean you were appointed and you didn't even know it? Someone had to tell you?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was not at the place where this executive board was nominated. I was told about this orally by Mr. Milos Bogdanovic, who was my boss. I was a professional in the field of civil protection before the war. I have decisions to that effect. And I was never invited to any meetings. Later, I don't know, a few months later, I saw this actual list of persons that you referred to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Including yourself?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I've explained. I've explained how and what.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, when you were informed that you had been appointed to this body without even being consulted, did you have any misgivings?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Chamber, if you know of any reason as to why it was that you were appointed to the executive board of this new Serbian municipality of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody discussed the proposal with me, and when I asked Milos Bogdanovic who nominated me, he said that he nominated me because I was a professional and qualified for defence matters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you want to be on the -- this executive board? Did you want to accept this appointment?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Milos Bogdanovic himself expressed his scepticism regarding this executive board.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. That's not the question. It's very simple. Did you want to be on it? Did you want to accept this appointment?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't want to be a member of that board.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I'll come back to the topic that I was dealing with before we got sidetracked into this issue of membership. This document, P112, even though it's a hollow document and relates to a non-functioning executive board, at least shows an intention on the part of the civilian authorities in Bosanski Samac to be kept informed by something called an executive body, executive board, to be kept informed of conditions on the ground in Bosanski Samac. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can agree if you are referring to the executive board where Mr. Milan Simic was president of the executive board.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. I'm just asking you this: This document, when you look at it, and read the articles, shows an intention to keep the Crisis Staff, the Serbian municipality of Bosanski Samac, informed of conditions within the municipality, because it reports -- it requires the executive board to report on the situation in all aspects of social life, does it not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the second time now, the Prosecutor, when putting his question, introduces the wrong term, that is to say that the executive board informs the Crisis Staff, and it says quite clearly that it is responsible to the Assembly and the Crisis Staff, so if he is referring to this field of information, because this article does not refer to information at all, only to responsibility, so could he clearly state what he is drawing on, please? MR. DI FAZIO: Certainly. Article 1, paragraph 2. "The executive board shall report to the Assembly, that is to the Crisis Staff of the Serbian municipality of Bosanski Samac, on the situation in all aspects of social life."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Maybe I have a solution, paragraph 2 of Article 1 of this decision, of this document, maybe it's something a problem with the translation. Maybe Mr. Ninkovic can read slowly paragraph 2 of the Article 1 of this decision and then we could clarify that, because according to the word in B/C/S version, then it is not inconsistent with the translation that we have in paragraph 2. So maybe in order to clarify our friends from the interpreters booth can clarify it. MR. DI FAZIO: I'll ask him to read it slowly that should solve the issue. I don't want to put matters to him if I've misunderstood the correct text.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you do that, please, Mr. Ninkovic, just read out slowly, paragraph 2 of Article 1?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I shall read paragraph 2 of Article 1.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could it please be put on the ELMO again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "The executive board reports to the Assembly, is accountable to the Assembly, or rather the Crisis Staff of the Serb Municipality of Bosanski Samac, for the situation in all fields of social life for the implementation of policies and the implementation of decisions and other regulations of the Assembly, i.e., the Crisis Staff of the Serb Municipality of Bosanski Samac."

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, because when we receive a translation of word "report" when my learned friend is using word "report," also witness is receiving the same word, which means is responsible or informed -- or report means in terms of informing one body, informing another body. And that's a confusion because the witness is not sure in which sense the question is posed. And for the record, from the part of Defence, we think that it is not an accurate translation of word in paragraph 2 of Article 1, that executive board shall report to the Assembly. We think that the right pronunciation and translation should be that executive board is responsible to the Assembly. MR. DI FAZIO: Mr. Weiner informs me that the use of the expression "shall report" is a deliberate use of the imperative, must report, shall, will report, and that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Does that mean is responsible to the assembly, as Mr. Pantelic says? MR. DI FAZIO: Well, I don't know and I'm not -- I don't want to go down that road. We've done the best that we can. It's been read out, you've got it there in black and white. It says, "Shall report." In any event for my purposes it really is a massive splitting of hairs and I don't need to go down that route any further. If Defence counsel want to clarify it, they can in re-examination.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One thing is clear, isn't it, whatever the form of words in paragraph 2 of Article 1, the point of it is that the executive board passes information, tells the Crisis Staff, on the situation in all fields of social life in the municipality? That's the stated intention in the document?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The words "to report" and the word "to be responsible" are words with different meanings in the Serbian language. To be responsible means to be responsible to a higher instance. The Assembly is a higher instance in relation to the executive board.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. We'll leave it at that. Let's have a look at Article 7. Rights and obligations of P112, please. Do you have it there? And just so that there is no problem --

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With that, just so there is no problem with language, can you just read out the first paragraph of Article 7? I don't need to have all of those numbers. Just read out the preamble and number 1.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Article 7?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "In carrying out its functions established by the constitution, law and other regulations of the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the executive board shall have the right and responsibility to:" You want me to read it up to there, right?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Number 1, just go on to number 1.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Point 1: "Monitor the situation in all fields of human activity and take measures to resolve questions in these fields."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Okay. That means, does it not, that the executive board had to be aware of conditions on the ground, the conditions existing in the Serbian municipality of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in terms of the competences of the executive board and the competences are specifically established by the Statute of the Municipal Assembly, that is to say, the competences of the executive board. That means that the executive board had to be aware of certain matters due to the very nature of its work, and on the other hand, they did not have to be aware of other things because that was not within the scope of their responsibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, Ms. Usher, I've finished with the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If there had been widespread looting of property in Bosanski Samac and in the municipality, that would be a matter that would be of the utmost concern to the Crisis Staff, would it not?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The public security station, the MUP that is, is supposed to be the first one to be informed of such situations, and then they should notify the executive board of the fact that looting had occurred. This is the mechanism of information between these authorities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for explaining the mechanism. If there had been widespread looting in the municipality of Bosanski Samac, that would be a matter of the utmost concern to the Crisis Staff, would it not? I'm not asking for the mechanism. I'm just asking you a very simple question. It would be a matter of the utmost concern to the Crisis Staff. Would you agree with that proposition?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You said "if looting had occurred, if major looting had occurred."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's right. You heard me correctly, you heard me absolutely correctly, Mr. Ninkovic. If that had happened, that would be a matter of the utmost concern to the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, are we here in the area of hypothetical questions and issues? Or we are trying to explore something factual?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, Mr. Pantelic, please sit down. Let the Prosecution continue. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, you would agree with me that if that had been the situation, it would have been a matter of the utmost concern to the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it had happened, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Certainly. If it had happened.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the right way to put that question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And if there had been mass arrests of Croat and Muslim men in the municipality of Bosanski Samac and in the town, that also would be a matter of the utmost concern to the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What does mass arrests mean? Does that mean a large number of persons brought into custody?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's say for argument's sake that if there had been mass arrests numbering in the hundreds, would that be a matter of the utmost concern to the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the Crisis Staff were to have such information, that could be looked at by the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm a bit concerned about your use of the expression "could." If the Crisis Staff had information about mass arrests of Croat and Muslim men numbering in the hundreds, that is something that the Crisis Staff would be most definitely be very concerned about, would it not?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can say that this word "could" is a word we could replace by the following: That such information should be on the agenda.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And similarly, if there had been such mass arrests and there had been torture and starvation and confinement under inhumane conditions, that similarly would be a matter of the utmost concern to the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to say that if there is knowledge of the kind you are referring to, in that case, yes. If there is knowledge concerning relevant information, if there are reports, if there is evidence, because such organs work according to materials that are prepared along with certain reports, information, relevant data.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Perhaps I can take you to an example of concern on the part of the Crisis Staff for the welfare of people. MR. DI FAZIO: Can the witness be shown Exhibit P99?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Firstly, are you familiar with that document?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's apparently signed by Dr. Blagoje Simic and dated the 17th of May, 1992, to the Federal Executive Council in Belgrade, and it shows, does it not, an awareness on the part of Dr. Blagoje Simic of the importance of compliance with international agreements on humanitarian issues, because he refers there to the Croatian side not complying with even the Geneva Conventions on the protection of civilians and prisoners of war and gives further detail, he refers to protocols 1 and 2. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And from what you know of Dr. Blagoje Simic, is it your position that he was a man who was concerned about humanitarian issues, the plight of civilians and prisoners of war, regardless of their ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you are talking about this figure of 3 and a half to 4.000 Serbs, I know with certainty that the largest number among them were women and children from Novi Grad, Dubica and Trnjak. Among them my father and my mother.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. My question is -- wasn't that. My question is: I'll be more precise to assist you. Did you ever see or hear anything that indicated on the part of Dr. Blagoje Simic the sort of humanitarian concerns he expresses in that letter?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Dr. Blagoje Simic here expressed his concern for these people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware if he shared the same concerns for non-Serbs?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With regard to that question, there is a difference. If you wish to compare people who were brought into custody at the public security station because of possession of weapons, or military materiel that is not allowed, then there is a difference between those persons and the persons referred to in this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. I'm not interested in any comparisons. Let me ask you, were you aware of any activity on the part of the Crisis Staff or the War Presidency or the Serbian municipality -- thank you, Ms. Usher, I've finished -- the municipality -- the Serbian municipality of Bosanski Samac, to detect any similar breaches of the Geneva Conventions within the municipality of Bosanski Samac? Were they in effect careful to root out the sort of activity that is being complained of in that letter, P99?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there were such activities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The distribution of bread, milk, I think and other food supplies. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I'm not quite certain of the times. What -- I'm happy to proceed, if you wish. On the other hand--

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. We will take a break for 20 minutes and continue at 1250 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio, continue. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, thank you, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just before the break I was asking you about Exhibit P99. I don't need to show it to you. Just let me tell you, remind you of what Dr. Blagoje Simic wrote. He complained of the civilian population exposed to physical terror, maltreatment, starvation, forced labour, and other methods of the most brutal execution. Now, are you aware of Dr. Blagoje Simic or the Crisis Staff adopting any measures or doing anything in the municipality of Bosanski Samac to stop precisely those sorts of things happening in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that civilian authorities tried to assist the civilian population when it came to creating basic necessities for life, distribution of food, potable water, and everything that we call the communal system, meaning utilities and everything, in order to create bearable living conditions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Can the witness be shown P79, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's an announcement dated the 17th of April, 1992. Are you familiar with that -- with that announcement?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let me ask you this: In the third paragraph, it says that the Crisis Staff guarantees -- "Shall guarantee the complete safety of life and property of citizens regardless of nationality and religion." Are you of anything else or do you have any information that confirms that the Crisis Staff guaranteed safety of life and property regardless nationality or religion?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see the paragraph that you read out here in this document; however, I don't know what is the origin of this document because I think that this document is questionable. It lacks a signature and I don't know whether this heading, which is handwritten, is authentic. Every document must have proper elements.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the stamps? Do the stamps look familiar?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a very bad copy or imprint. I don't know what the original is like. But somebody else could have produced this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you got any reason to disagree with the proposition that the Crisis Staff guaranteed the safety of life and property to citizens regardless of their nationality and religion?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We've talked about this before. I think that every kind of authority is based on those principles, if it is a democratic one, and upholds the rule of law.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were closely associated with the press, of course, in April of 1992, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As an employee in the information service, I engaged in journalistic activities and I had contact with various media outlets, if that's what you have in mind, and information agencies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of Simeon Simic ever sending this document to the press?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry, can you just recapitulate now about what it is about this document that causes you to cast doubt on its authenticity?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In view of the fact that I'm an employee of the state administration, that I've had experience with that, I can tell you right away that this is a typewritten document, that the heading is handwritten, that the imprint of this stamp is unclear and that there is no signature; therefore, the document is questionable.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. But other than that, you have no direct information or otherwise as to whether or not this is an authentic document?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I cannot give evidence regarding that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If it was a real document, an authentic document, would Simeon Simic have had cause to send it to the press?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, no. In view of the answers from the witness, you can't ask him that question. MR. DI FAZIO: Very well, I'll withdraw the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were announcements of the Crisis Staff sent to the press from time to time?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, there was a proclamation or announcement or something like that addressed to Tanug and it dealt with the status of Serbs in Odzak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Okay, thank you. Can I take you to a fresh document now, please? MR. DI FAZIO: Can the witness be shown Exhibit D61/1?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Di Fazio, could I have a clarification of what Tanug is? MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Line 13, please. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You heard Her Honour's question, am I correct that it's some sort of news agency? You nodded but for the transcript we need to have a yes or a no so that we -- an audible yes or no?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will explain. Tanug is an abbreviation, and it stands for Telegraph Agency of New Yugoslavia. It is a news agency created after World War II in the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia immediately after the Second World War. It was the most influential news agency which was the source of information for other media outlets.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you very much. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, D61. This was a Defence document introduced into evidence. You've seen this document, I believe.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We've analysed this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Right. And it's essentially a complaint against soldiers cutting down trees or woods and threatening workers, forestry workers or whatever.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you expecting an answer from me?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. You agree with that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In order to prevent such criminal events, a military organ is responsible for that because this has to do with members of the military. Therefore, commander of the unit is responsible for taking measures through military police and various military organs in order to prevent this from happening, because the Prosecution for these cases is in the hands of the military, because these are members of the military.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fine. That's -- I don't want to go into this chapter and verse but essentially, this fellow, Stevan Tutnjevic complained about soldiers cutting down trees and sent copies of this letter with its complaint to the executive board, the president of the municipality, Dr. Blagoje Simic, the police and so on; right?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But Mr. Stevan Tutnjevic is probably not aware of the system of responsibilities and competences, so due to his ignorance, he sent this letter to wrong institutions. Had Mr. Tutnjevic known that the commander of the unit is in charge of investigating this, he would have sent it to the commander, not to these institutions mentioned here, although I can see here that he sent this to the military police as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fine. Now, did the Crisis Staff and the -- let me put it more generally, the civilian authorities in Bosanski Samac act upon this? Did they try and do something to help out Stevan Tutnjevic? Did they do something it try to help out the cutting or prevent, rather, the cutting of trees and woods, to try and do something about the problem? To lend their support and help?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you have in mind that this document was sent to the department of the defence, I personally can tell you what the situation is with respect to myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. I'm not interested in whether it was sent to the department of defence. I'm interested in a really very simple little matter. It's very simple. Not complicated. There is a complaint about soldiers cutting down trees. Did the Crisis Staff try to do, and the civilian authorities, try to do something to help in respect of this problem, to do something to protect the forests?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do apologise, maybe in order to avoid confusing matter, because this letter was made in 1993 and there is not any mention of the Crisis Staff here. Maybe my learned friend can specify the body, if he's speaking about this. MR. DI FAZIO: I said civilian authorities. I said civilian authorities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let me repeat the question, Mr. Ninkovic. There is a complaint here about soldiers cutting down woods. Did the civilian authorities, whatever particular incarnation they had at the time, did the civilian authorities try and do something to help this man, to help the woods and forests from being cut down?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they tried to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you recall what they did?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They established contact with the commanders of the units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And presumably raised the issue with them, discussed the issue with them, tried to find a solution? I'm sorry, I didn't hear any answer. Did you say yes or no?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't say anything because I didn't hear you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry, I'll repeat my question. I asked you if you recall what they did, you said they contacted the commanders of the units, and my question to you is this: Presumably, the civilian authorities raised the issue, this issue of the cutting down of wood, with the military authorities and tried to come to some sort of solution or to deal with the problem.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Organs of civilian authorities of Samac municipality had contacts with commanders of units in that area regarding this issue and they explained the problem to them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And presumably, therefore, if soldiers or paramilitaries are slaughtering people, the Crisis Staff could do something about it by at least contacting military units in much the same way as they did to protect forests?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps a clarification is in order. See, we don't have to predict or forecast the powers of civilian authorities here. Those who had an opportunity to be in a certain area that was encircled during wartime would know that all of the power during that time is concentrated in the arms of the military and that the military at that time usually has an arrogant attitude and manifests its powers with respect to those who are weaker and in this case, it is the civilian authorities who are weaker. And this is how it was with the military circles in Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But with respect, just answer my question. If paramilitaries are slaughtering people, for example killing 15 or 16 people in a wheat factory in Crkvina, there is absolutely nothing, is there, to stop the Crisis Staff from at least writing a letter or telephoning the military authorities, doing something, to try and find some sort of solution to the problem, to deal with it?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The question is whether the Crisis Staff had that information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you saying that the Crisis Staff didn't know about the murder of 15 or 16 people at Crkvina? Is that your position?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I'm trying to say is that I don't know whether the Crisis Staff had that information. I was not a member of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. And now let's return to my question for the third time. Is there anything that you can think of that would have prevented the Crisis Staff from contacting the military authorities in a formal or informal manner and doing something to come to grips with this problem of the slaughter of Croat and Muslim civilians?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I can answer that question. The situation in that area was not the same in different periods of time. With the arrival of the 1st Krajina Corps, which is a large military power which had within itself half of the members of the Army of Republika Srpska, and Mile Beronja was appointed as commander of the 2nd Posavina Brigade, I think that must have been in August or September, then the other commanders from within the Krajina corps arrived, the second Krajina Brigade and other units that existed within that corps. So with these professionals, one could have a reasonable conversation. And as to the volunteers that you mentioned, any contact with them was dangerous. Those were the people who were not familiar with law, with regulations, customs of war and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The mass murder of 15 or 16 people, of Croat and Muslim ethnicity, by a member of Serbian military forces is a matter that would cause considerable unrest, fear in the non-Serb population, if it became known. Would you agree with that, the non-Serb population of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with you that that was a crime and I can only express my deepest condolences to the families of those who had been murdered. I spoke to you about the context of relationship between the civilian authorities and the volunteers. The contact between them was not always possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Ninkovic, I'm not asking you to express condolences or anything like that. It's very simple -- it's a very simple question. The slaughter of 15 or 16 non-Serb people by a member of the Serb military forces would be a matter of the utmost concern to the non-Serb population living then, back then, in 1992, in Bosanski Samac, if it became known? That must inevitably be so, wouldn't you agree?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That case is in the hands of the military security, the MUP, military prosecution and military judiciary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, all right. Okay. Well, we'll leave the matter at that. MR. DI FAZIO: Can the witness be shown D62/1? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you I think are familiar with this document, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a minute, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You looked at it yesterday but please refresh your memory.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, the document of course is from Blagoje Simic to the President of the republic, General Mladic, Defence Minister, Commander of the 1st Krajina Corps, and essentially it complains of larceny and pilferage and robbery committed by members of the 1st Krajina Corps. Do you see that? That's the essence of the document, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can see what it is about based on this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's a complaint about the behaviour of soldiers in respect of larceny and pilfering and looting; right? Complaint about the behaviour of Serbian soldiers. And is therefore an example of Dr. Blagoje Simic doing something to alleviate the problem caused by the behaviour of soldiers. That is correct, is it not?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what the consequences of this letter were. I don't know what effective measures --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about the consequences --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can you pay attention to the question and simply answer the question? Don't go ahead of the question. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. I'm grateful to Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about the consequence. It's a very simple matter. It's basically a complaint by Dr. Blagoje Simic to state organs and military -- and the military about the behaviour of soldiers in respect of looting and pilfering and so on. That's the essence of the document, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that from the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fine. Now, if Dr. Blagoje Simic can write a letter of complaint to the republic president and General Mladic, the commander of the 1st Krajina Corps, complaining about such matters, there is nothing, is there, to prevent him writing a similar letter in respect of the slaughter of 15 or 16 people in Crkvina. Nothing that springs to mind, anyway.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not agree, because there is a rational explanation for this. This is a document from 1993. 1993. The crime that you refer to occurred in 1992. Mr. Blagoje Simic could have been killed by those men who had committed this crime if they were to find out that he had complained to someone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The man -- you know that the man who killed the people at Crkvina was a fellow named Lugar. You know that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was still wandering around at -- and at large, in 1993, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Well, let me ask you about 1992. Are you saying that something like D62/1 could never have been sent because if Lugar and his associates had discovered of such a complaint, Dr. Blagoje Simic's life would have been in danger? Is that the reason?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wish to say precisely that. Namely, if they were to find out that Dr. Blagoje Simic had complained to someone who was more powerful and above him, then his life would have been in danger.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware if he considered writing a letter such as D62/1 in respect of the Crkvina murders?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: D62/1 is essentially concerned about larceny and pilferage and robbery of Serbian property, isn't it, property owned by Serbs?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the middle of the first page, it says, in big, capital letters, "The Serb army is looting Serb property."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So your answer is yes; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That can be seen from the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you aware of there having been any similar problems in respect of property held by non-Serbs?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Criminals do not know of the origin of property. They just know what the object of their looting is. That is a general characteristic of criminals in any state and in any system.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it the case that the Crisis Staff and the later in the year the War Presidency, was completely unable to do anything about the behaviour of paramilitaries in the municipality of Bosanski Samac in 1992?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It can be put that way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This was a serious undermining of its power and authority, was it not?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It can be interpreted that way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if civilian governments have their power and authority undermined, they have to do something about that normally, don't they?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I want to say the following to you, and I have already spoken about that. This is the period of 1992. A few months into the war. This is a period that is marked by the need to develop institutions. That is to say the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina had not had a developed internal state structure yet. Real power was in the hands of those who had weapons and military force. Those who did not have that, those who had official appointments, that was controversial from the point of view of power, you see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Doesn't that fly in the face of the evidence that you've given to this Chamber in the last two or three days? You have been at pains, haven't you, to point out that procedures were followed strictly, that legislation was adhered to, to the letter, that there were clear demarcations between government departments, for example, demarcation between the Ministry of the Defence and the Crisis Staff, that people's jobs were clearly defined? Now, are you saying that that wasn't the case at all and it was rather a state of anarchy that existed in the municipality whereby people like Lugar and his associates held real power?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You draw the wrong conclusion from my evidence here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but can you answer the question?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you look at my documents, the ones I signed here, and they were shown, every document was based on the law. It had clear form, clear legal form, and substance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Can I ask you this? Were you ever a member of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I've already said that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you eventually a member of a functioning, real, existent executive board?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we are talking about the executive board from 1993, which was appointed on the basis of the change of the statute of the Municipal Assembly, in which it says that the head of department is ex officio a member when defence matters are discussed, then I can say yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. You essentially took over the position of Milos Bogdanovic in the executive board after he left; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. I did not take over the Secretary for National Defence. This was a municipal organ. While the department of the Ministry of Defence was a republic organ. I was appointed by Mr. Subotic, Minister of Defence, to be head of the department of Ministry of Defence and there is a difference in the levels of these institutions. I'll remind you that the law on defence came out on the 1st of June. It was published on the 8th of June. And all of these things that we are discussing now are derived from that law. I testified about that in great detail over these past few days, with very precise notions and qualifications from this particular law.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. MR. DI FAZIO: Can the witness be shown Exhibits P86 and P87?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Firstly, let me ask you to look at both documents and acquaint yourself with the contents. Do you have that?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I read this first item, the decision.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fine. Now, the decision appointing you, P86, that says that you're going to be secretary for the municipal Secretariat for National Defence; right?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I clearly interpreted yesterday the fact that this document should be taken as a proposal. If you look at this here, I think it's the 13th or 18th of June, then the Crisis Staff did not know yet, or did not have the law on defence yet, the one that had just come out. While the Minister of Defence asked for a proposal for a nomination to this post, that is to say head of department. That is a republic organ. I have a decision made by the minister in terms of this appointment and I can have it and it says there that the Minister of Defence on the basis of the proposals that came in appoints Bozo Ninkovic, that is yours truly, to be head of department of the Ministry of Defence in Bosanski Samac and this is the 16th of July, 1992. That is when the Secretariat for Defence expired as such, while a new republic organ came into being. That is the department of defence. And by virtue of my appointment of -- as head of department, it is believed that the defence department of the municipality of Samac was constituted. And there is yet another document in this regard that I can show.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Exactly I would like to have just a small intervention to the transcript. It's page 83, line 18, this witness is speaking about his appointment and then he said, "I can have it." Which is not particularly in line what he just said. In fact, then he said, "I can show it if it's necessary," meaning this decision of appointment because again he stated that he can show it. So it's up to the Prosecution or maybe this Trial Chamber if there is any need to clarify that issue. My understanding is that the witness is in possession of this document so he can submit it to the proceedings. Yes, thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, P--

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It's up to the Prosecution to clear that up if they wish to. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, thank you, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: P87, also clearly relieves Milos Bogdanovic as secretary of the municipal Secretariat for National Defence. Do you see that? I'm not asking you to give us another explanation of the republican laws, just what the document says.

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you are talking about this document on his relieving of office, it can be seen that Milos Bogdanovic is being relieved of this office because he's going to another office. This is the 14th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fine. Now, was he a member of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For you to carry out your duties back then, in 1992, for you to be a competent, fully functioning official in the Ministry of the Defence, given the wartime conditions, it would have been essential for you to know who was on the Crisis Staff, would it not? It would have been essential for you to know just who headed up the civilian authorities?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can speak about certain persons in terms of that I think that they were there, but I never saw decidedly a list. I'm trying to say that the notion of the Crisis Staff as for its composition and decision making, that people went to this Crisis Staff depending on the circumstances involved and the subject that the Crisis Staff was dealing with. So different people over there discussed different subjects at different times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Might I ask for the documents just to remain with the witness, and Ms. Usher can perhaps sit down? One thing is for sure: One of the people best qualified to speak about membership of the Crisis Staff would be a member of the Crisis Staff themselves? That must be so?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Logically.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Incidentally, do you know if Stevan Todorovic was a member of the Crisis Staff at any time?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry, just to be absolutely clear, what you're saying is you don't know, or no, he was not a member?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I'm not aware of that. MR. DI FAZIO: Would Your Honours bear with me for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We still need clarification because in English it's not clear which way. You were not aware that Stevan Todorovic was a member of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that I was not a member of the Crisis Staff, and from there, I draw a logical conclusion that only who was a member of the Crisis Staff can testify to exactly who was a member of the Crisis Staff. So I am not aware of Stevan Todorovic being a member of the Crisis Staff. MR. DI FAZIO: I apologise, Your Honour, I've just temporarily mislaid a note. My I just be given a moment, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Mr. Miroslav Tadic a member of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure. I think he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was interviewed by officers of the Office of the Prosecutor back in the late 1990s, and when he was being questioned by those investigators, he was asked about membership of the Crisis Staff and he said that Milos Bogdanovic was a member of the Crisis Staff by virtue of his being chief of the Secretariat of National Defence. Did the same apply to you after you went to the Ministry of Defence?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of being head of the Ministry of Defence in Bosanski Samac entitling you to membership of the Crisis Staff, if you wished to join?

utterances.speaker: BOZO NINKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I explained my position, and the hierarchy in the Ministry of Defence; that is to say, that my responsibility was vis-a-vis the Minister of Defence of the Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Similarly, in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We have reached our time because the room will be occupied by another trial. So we have to adjourn.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may on behalf of my colleagues in the -- and my clients to wish Merry Christmas to all the colleagues and everybody here and Happy New Year. Maybe our friends in the Prosecution can drop the charges in the new year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ninkovic, we haven't finished with your evidence. Cross-examination will continue on the 8th of January at 1415 hours next year.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have been here for 25 days now. Today is my 23rd day. I would just like to ask the following: When I am asked to come here again for these proceedings, may I not stay very long? I have my work. I have my family. I kindly request this Court to make it possible for me to spend as short time as possible here because I have been here for very long now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber was not aware that you've been here for close to a month. That is really -- anyway, we don't know why you stayed for so long. MR. DI FAZIO: I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, you had two hours 15 minutes. MR. DI FAZIO: I'll need more time, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: How much? You heard the witness that he wants to know. MR. DI FAZIO: I'm mindful of that. I want to cut down what I've got to an absolute minimum. If Your Honours please, the situation with members -- high ranking members in the civilian administration in -- who are being called as witnesses has changed as time has gone on. A lot more documents have been produced into evidence than was the case, for example, when Mr. Mirko Lukic first gave his evidence, and so my cross-examination will have to be, I submit, of -- longer than it was in the case of those two previous witnesses simply even because of the increased volume of documentation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, Mr. Di Fazio, that can't be a reason because you have to look at your case. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We have a specific case here. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And that is the case you seek to strengthen through cross-examination. MR. DI FAZIO: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You don't increase the hours simply because there are many documents. Some of the documents are not of any use at all. MR. DI FAZIO: Precisely. Precisely. If Your Honours pleases, I have no quarrel with that. I understand that, and much of it won't be of concern to us. I'm not going sit here and go through each and every document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no, no. The Trial Chamber will give you another period of three hours. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: To complete your cross-examination. And then re-examination and then the witness can go. Because that way the witness can only spend two days, if we start on the 8th, then on the 9th, he should be finished. MR. DI FAZIO: Well, two days would be -- I would think would be quite enough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, but I'm saying you have three hours when we resume next year so you better reorganise your cross-examination. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. The Trial Chamber also wishes everybody a safe and happy holiday. We will rise now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 8th day of January, 2003. 21 22 23 24 25
